question: A patient with stable blood pressure keeps coming back, demanding brain scans because they are convinced they have a fatal tumour, despite clear test results. What is this called?

options.A: Health anxiety
options.B: Symptom denial
options.C: Stoic endurance
options.D: Normal recovery

explanation: When someone constantly worries they have a severe illness despite all medical proof to the contrary, it points toward health anxiety.

question: Why do many terminal patients and their families choose home-based palliative care?

options.A: It guarantees that the terminal illness will suddenly go into full remission
options.B: It allows the patient to spend time in a familiar environment with loved ones
options.C: It is completely free with zero financial planning required
options.D: It removes the need for any nursing involvement whatsoever

explanation: Being at home offers comfort and surrounds the patient with familiar people and belongings during end-of-life stages. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h5)

question: What advice should you give a patient receiving treatment for a bacterial STI regarding sex?

options.A: Resume intercourse immediately once the burning sensation starts to fade
options.B: Limit intercourse to protected methods without needing partner treatment
options.C: Abstain from sexual activity until he and his partner have finished treatment
options.D: Use oil-based lubricants to prevent transmission while taking oral tablets

explanation: No sex until both partners finish their treatment course! This stops the dreaded 'ping-pong' effect of passing the infection right back to each other.

question: Which of these is a very common female-related cause of infertility?

options.A: Permanent enlargement of the prostate gland
options.B: Hyperactive sperm motility within the uterus
options.C: Complete absence of the pituitary hormone testosterone
options.D: Tubal blockages from previous pelvic infections

explanation: Past untreated infections (like PID) can leave scars or blockages in the fallopian tubes, stopping the egg and sperm from meeting.

question: Why are deep breathing exercises so important for a patient stuck on bed rest in traction?

options.A: They relax tight muscles to stop spasms
options.B: They stimulate blood flow inside the deep calf veins
options.C: They expand the lungs fully to prevent mucus buildup and collapse
options.D: They increase the pulling force of the traction weights

explanation: Thinking like a real nurse! Lying in bed slows down breathing, which can cause lung issues. Deep breaths keep the tiny air sacs open and clear out mucus.

question: Why do we use a clean razor blade from a birth kit to cut the baby's cord?

options.A: To speed up the drying of the remaining cord stump
options.B: To make the procedure painless for the newborn baby
options.C: To prevent tetanus and other bacterial infections
options.D: To ensure the cord detaches within the first 24 hours

explanation: Using a clean, sterile blade stops nasty germs from getting into the fresh cord vessels. That's our main defense against neonatal tetanus! You've got this.

question: A maternity nurse ignores a fetal monitor beep because too many false alarms sounded earlier. What is this called?

options.A: Fixation error
options.B: Memory lapse
options.C: Confirmation bias
options.D: Alert fatigue

explanation: Well done! When machines beep too often for nothing, we get 'alert fatigue' and might sadly miss the one time the alarm is actually saving a life.

question: Why does clearing stagnant water around homes help stop disease?

options.A: It stops soil erosion during heavy rainfall
options.B: It purifies the underground water table naturally
options.C: It removes the breeding grounds for mosquito vectors
options.D: It prevents the spread of airborne tuberculosis droplets

explanation: Spot on! Mosquitoes love to lay eggs in quiet, stagnant pools. Clearing them out breaks their life cycle and keeps malaria at bay.

question: Why is long-term sustainability such an important goal for community health programs?

options.A: It guarantees that nurses will receive permanent salary increases from the state
options.B: It ensures health promotion continues after external project funding eventually stops
options.C: It prevents infectious disease outbreaks from occurring in urban slums
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for future community health assessments

explanation: Spot on! External grants and projects eventually end. Building local community leadership ensures that the good work keeps going long after outsiders leave.

question: A community health nurse notices high rates of typhoid in a rural village. Which intervention best addresses the underlying determinant of health?

options.A: Writing a research paper on the biology of the typhoid bacterium
options.B: Partnering with local leaders to build protected boreholes for clean water
options.C: Telling every resident to boil their drinking water for five minutes
options.D: Opening a large tertiary hospital in the nearest capital city

explanation: Addressing the root environmental determinant, such as unsafe water infrastructure, provides a long-term solution to waterborne disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the main use of short-acting beta-agonists (SABAs) in asthma care?

options.A: Preventing mucus production over a twenty-four hour period
options.B: Providing quick relief during sudden acute bronchospasm
options.C: Curing the underlying chronic inflammation in the lungs
options.D: Rebuilding damaged lung tissue caused by frequent infections

explanation: SABAs act fast during sudden breathlessness, which is why patients carry them around as their reliable rescue inhalers.

question: What happens to most of the developing follicles in the ovary during a typical cycle?

options.A: They turn directly into the corpus luteum
options.B: They migrate into the fallopian tubes
options.C: They all release eggs simultaneously
options.D: They degenerate through atresia

explanation: Even though a group of follicles starts growing each month, only one becomes the champion (dominant) follicle. The rest quietly break down through a natural process called atresia.

question: What is the main difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?

options.A: If they come from plant or animal sources
options.B: How fast they dissolve in the bloodstream
options.C: The total amount the body requires daily
options.D: Whether they can provide energy to the body

explanation: You got it! Macro means large (needed in grams), while micro means small (needed in tiny milligram or microgram amounts).

question: How many sections make up the abdominopelvic quadrant system?
explanation: The abdominopelvic area is split into four quadrants for rapid clinical screening during assessments. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which part of the ovary holds the developing egg follicles?

options.A: Medulla
options.B: Cortex
options.C: Fimbria
options.D: Fundus

explanation: The outer layer, or cortex, contains ovarian follicles in different stages of growth and maturation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the final active form of vitamin D made by the kidneys?

options.A: Ergocalciferol
options.B: Cholecalciferol
options.C: Cholesterol
options.D: Calcitriol

explanation: You're doing great! The kidneys put the finishing touch on vitamin D by turning it into calcitriol, which keeps your bones strong and healthy.

question: Which food nutrients are most important for keeping bones strong and posture upright?

options.A: Sodium and potassium
options.B: Vitamin C and iron
options.C: Protein and zinc
options.D: Calcium and vitamin D

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D are the ultimate dynamic duo for bone health! They build strong bones and help prevent weakness or spinal curving.

question: Why do we give a routine injection of Vitamin K to all newborns shortly after birth?

options.A: To boost their appetite for milk
options.B: To prevent dangerous bleeding since their clotting factors are low
options.C: To protect against hepatitis B
options.D: To protect against eye infections from the birth canal

explanation: Babies are born with sterile bellies that haven't built up the gut bacteria needed to make Vitamin K yet, putting them at risk for bleeding until feeding gets going.

question: If you delegate a routine task to a nursing assistant as a registered nurse, who still holds the ultimate legal responsibility?

options.A: The hospital ward manager on duty
options.B: The nursing assistant who performed the task
options.C: The registered nurse who made the delegation
options.D: The physician in charge of the patient

explanation: Remember this rule: you can delegate tasks, but you can never delegate ultimate accountability. As the RN, you supervise and check the final outcome!

question: What is the main way that antiemetic (anti-nausea) drugs stop vomiting?

options.A: Blocking specific neurotransmitter receptors
options.B: Destroying circulating toxins in the blood
options.C: Enhancing gastric motility and emptying
options.D: Increasing blood flow to the medulla oblongata

explanation: You nailed it! Anti-nausea meds work by latching onto and blocking the chemical receptors along the vomiting pathway so the brain doesn't get the 'throw up' signal. Keep it up!

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for rectal medication administration?

options.A: Mild high blood pressure
options.B: Mild headache and body fatigue
options.C: History of seasonal allergies
options.D: Recent rectal or bowel surgery

explanation: Inserting a suppository into a healing surgical site can damage tissue, cause pain, and disrupt sutures. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h6)

question: What happens during the T wave of a normal heartbeat?

options.A: The main heart valves snap shut to trap blood inside
options.B: The electrical signal fires off inside the sinus node
options.C: Blood rushes rapidly from the body into the right atrium
options.D: The ventricles recharge and get ready for the next beat

explanation: The T wave marks ventricular repolarization, which is the electrical recovery or resting state of the lower chambers. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h2)

question: What do we call a patient who keeps shedding germs even after they've started feeling better?

options.A: Incubation carrier
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Acute clinical case
options.D: Convalescent carrier

explanation: A convalescent carrier is someone who is recovering and feeling good again, but their body is still letting out a few leftover germs.

question: What is the main cause of an ischemic stroke?

options.A: Sudden systemic drop in normal body temperature
options.B: Uncontrolled electrical discharge across the motor cortex
options.C: Rupture of a weakened blood vessel inside the brain tissue
options.D: Occlusion of a cerebral artery by a thrombus or embolus

explanation: An ischemic stroke happens when a blood clot blocks a brain vessel, cutting off the oxygen and nutrients that part of the brain needs.

question: Between these patients, who is most at risk of developing constipation from slowed body movement?

options.A: A nursing student drinking several cups of coffee daily
options.B: A young athlete who drinks water after a football match
options.C: An older adult on strict bed rest after hip surgery
options.D: A patient with a mild viral stomach flu and loose stools

explanation: Well done! Staying in bed without moving, especially as we grow older, slows down natural bowel activity and makes constipation a major risk.

question: What is the main focus of a community diagnosis?

options.A: The administrative duties of senior doctors
options.B: The recovery rate of a single patient
options.C: The financial budget of a local hospital
options.D: The health status of a whole population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks broadly at the health and living conditions of an entire community rather than focusing on one individual patient. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h1)

question: How do nurses usually record how much of a meal a patient actually ate in the chart?

options.A: Counting every individual grain of rice
options.B: Taking a photo of the tray after eating
options.C: Weighing food scraps on a gram scale
options.D: Percentage estimation of the meal eaten

explanation: That's right! We estimate intake in quarters (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) to quickly track how much nourishment they got.

question: A patient has severe laryngitis with a painful, raspy voice and is given steam inhalation. What is the main goal here?

options.A: To deliver systemic antibiotics directly into the bloodstream
options.B: To force deep lung expansion in the lower alveoli
options.C: To soothe inflamed vocal cords and mucosal tissues
options.D: To permanently cure the viral infection overnight

explanation: You got it! Moist heat hydrates dry, raw throat tissues, taking away that scratchy irritation and giving sore vocal cords a chance to rest and heal.

question: A family member is feeding a stroke survivor who can actually hold a spoon with an adaptive grip. What should you do?

options.A: Recommend switching the patient entirely to liquid nutritional supplements
options.B: Praise the family member for providing thorough and efficient care
options.C: Insist that the nurse take over all feeding duties moving forward
options.D: Encourage the patient to use the adaptive spoon independently during meals

explanation: We always want to cheer patients on to do as much as they can for themselves. Independence speeds up recovery!

question: What main process causes tissue damage inside the pancreas during acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Infection of pancreatic tissue by gut bacteria traveling upward
options.B: Rapid formation of scar tissue blocking the pancreatic duct
options.C: Autodigestion of the pancreas by its own early-activated enzymes
options.D: Complete lack of blood supply caused by sudden heart failure

explanation: Think of it as friendly fire! Digestive enzymes turn on too early while still inside the pancreas, and they accidentally start breaking down the organ's own tissue.

question: When do we typically expect a secondary postpartum haemorrhage to happen?

options.A: During the immediate pushing of the placenta
options.B: Only after the baby stops breastfeeding completely
options.C: Within the first two hours after a CS
options.D: Between 24 hours and six weeks after delivery

explanation: Secondary PPH shows up later—anytime from 24 hours up to six weeks postpartum. It's usually caused by tiny bits of leftover tissue or an infection.

question: A patient with a recent stroke begins leaking stool unconsciously. What is the most likely underlying cause?

options.A: Primary infection of the internal anal lining
options.B: Neurological damage disrupting normal bowel signaling
options.C: Complete loss of rectal tissue elasticity
options.D: Severe physical injury to the external sphincter muscle

explanation: Strokes affect the central nervous system pathways that control voluntary bowel function, leading to reflex emptying without conscious control. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: Your patient cannot afford the wound care supplies you prescribed. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell the client to stop changing the dressing until they find money
options.B: Buy all the medical supplies using personal out-of-pocket funds
options.C: Discharge the client from home care services for non-compliance
options.D: Connect the client with a social worker or local community assistance program

explanation: Brilliant! Poverty is a barrier, not disobedience. Linking them with social welfare or community programs helps find practical financial support.

question: How long does standard multidrug therapy (MDT) last for multibacillary leprosy?

options.A: Twelve to twenty-four months
options.B: Five years or lifelong
options.C: Exactly six months
options.D: Two to four weeks

explanation: Correct! Multibacillary cases need a longer treatment stretch, usually 12 to 24 months, to clear the heavy germ load.

question: What essential instruction must be given about sexual partners when treating infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Partners can continue unprotected intercourse during the treatment week.
options.B: Partners only need treatment if they develop severe abdominal pain.
options.C: Only partners with visible symptoms need prescription medication.
options.D: Sexual partners must be checked and treated at the same time.

explanation: Treating partners together is the only way to stop the annoying ping-pong game of passing the infection back and forth!

question: What makes a female Guinea worm burst open and release her babies into water?

options.A: Exposure to sunlight
options.B: Ingestion of antibiotics
options.C: High fever in the host
options.D: Contact with cold water

explanation: Correct! When an infected person steps into a pond or well, the cool water signals the worm to release her larvae. You're mastering the transmission cycle!

question: A rural health clinic has only two nurses on duty. Which staffing approach ensures the best care for the community?

options.A: Firing the nurses and hiring administrative clerks
options.B: Employing polyvalent nurses trained in multiple care areas
options.C: Restricting care strictly to adult male patients
options.D: Closing the clinic until a specialist doctor arrives

explanation: Spot on! Having polyvalent nurses means a small team can safely and confidently handle a wide variety of health needs in the community.

question: How does risk pooling benefit hospitals within the HMO framework?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever getting sick again
options.B: It guarantees a steady and predictable flow of income for operations
options.C: It allows them to charge any price they want for surgery
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses and doctors

explanation: By collecting regular fees from many enrollees, the HMO ensures hospitals receive consistent payments instead of depending on erratic cash from individual patients. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h2)

question: When is a closed-ended question most helpful during an assessment?

options.A: When starting the orientation phase of an admission
options.B: When you need a quick, specific fact like a drug allergy
options.C: When you want the patient to describe their life story
options.D: When the patient is feeling anxious and needs to vent

explanation: Correct! Closed questions are great when you just need quick, straight-to-the-point facts like dates, numbers, or allergies.

question: Which of these is a common, validated questionnaire used by healthcare workers to measure a person's stress levels?

options.A: Perceived Stress Scale
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Apgar Score
options.D: Braden Scale

explanation: The Perceived Stress Scale is a handy tool clinicians use to understand how overwhelmed or stressed a person is feeling. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h5)

question: How many days does normal menstrual bleeding usually last?

options.A: 11 to 14 days
options.B: 1 to 2 days
options.C: 8 to 10 days
options.D: 3 to 7 days

explanation: A normal period generally lasts anywhere from 3 to 7 days. Knowing this helps you reassure patients in the clinic!

question: Why must you remove a medication patch from a patient's chest before putting on AED pads?

options.A: The medication will instantly enter the machine and break the processor.
options.B: The patch makes the skin too slippery for the rescuer to press hard.
options.C: The patch will absorb the conductive gel and ruin the AED pads.
options.D: The patch can block the electrical current and cause skin burns.

explanation: Medication patches can interfere with the electricity and even cause nasty skin burns. Always peel them off and wipe the skin clean first!

question: What are the three categories assessed in the standard Glasgow Coma Scale?

options.A: Reflexes, muscle tone, and sensation
options.B: Pupil reaction, blood pressure, and heart rate
options.C: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.D: Swallowing, speech, and balance

explanation: The GCS evaluates three distinct behavioral domains: how the eyes open, what the patient says, and how the body moves. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the biggest advantage of using local community radio stations for NCD health campaigns?

options.A: They replace the need for physical clinical screening examinations
options.B: They can broadcast messages in indigenous languages to reach remote areas
options.C: They are exclusively funded by international public health organizations
options.D: They guarantee that every listener will immediately adopt a healthy diet

explanation: Spot on! Radio bridges the gap, bringing vital health messages right into homes and farms using the local dialects people speak every day.

question: Why should a nurse place a convulsing patient in the side-lying recovery position?

options.A: To completely stop the rhythmic shaking of the lower limbs
options.B: To prevent the patient from rolling off the examination bed
options.C: To allow saliva and vomit to drain out and prevent choking
options.D: To make it easier to administer intravenous medications in the arm

explanation: Brilliant! The side-lying position lets saliva or vomit drain safely out of the mouth so the airway stays clear.

question: What is the primary surgical treatment for uterine cancer?

options.A: Total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
options.B: Partial resection of the uterine cervix only
options.C: Removal of both ovaries while leaving the uterus intact
options.D: Cryotherapy and laser ablation of the endometrium

explanation: You got it! Standard surgery means taking out the uterus, Fallopian tubes, and ovaries to treat the cancer safely.

question: Which nursing check is most critical immediately after a patient returns from a tubal ligation procedure?

options.A: Assessing the client's ability to conceive within one month
options.B: Testing the patient for signs of future fertility recovery
options.C: Measuring exact daily caloric intake and urinary output
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and assessing the abdominal incision site

explanation: Immediate post-operative care centers on recovery from anesthesia, stable vital signs, and watching for bleeding or complications at the surgical site. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h5)

question: Why should a nurse give written discharge instructions about pain meds to a recovering patient?

options.A: It replaces the need for any verbal conversation entirely
options.B: Written papers are legally required to keep nurses from being sued
options.C: Patients often forget verbal instructions due to stress and fatigue
options.D: Pharmacies will not sell pain medication without hospital paper

explanation: When people are stressed or tired, details slip their minds. Written guides are lifesavers for safe home care!

question: Which blood pressure drugs are strictly avoided in pregnancy because they harm fetal kidneys?

options.A: ACE inhibitors
options.B: Calcium channel blockers
options.C: Central alpha agonists
options.D: Beta blockers

explanation: ACE inhibitors (like enalapril or lisinopril) can cause serious kidney and skull damage to the baby, so doctors steer clear of them during pregnancy.

question: Which two brain chemicals are mainly responsible for balancing excitation and inhibition?

options.A: Acetylcholine and epinephrine
options.B: Dopamine and serotonin
options.C: Norepinephrine and histamine
options.D: Glutamate and GABA

explanation: Think of glutamate as the gas pedal (excitatory) and GABA as the brake pedal (inhibitory). Keeping them balanced keeps the brain stable!

question: Why must nurses strongly advise patients never to stop their anti-anxiety medications abruptly?

options.A: The medication will spoil if left in the bottle for too long.
options.B: Sudden discontinuation can cause severe withdrawal symptoms and a return of anxiety.
options.C: Doctors charge extra fees if a prescription is finished early.
options.D: Abrupt stopping causes the patient to forget their daily schedule.

explanation: Stopping psychiatric drugs cold turkey can shock the nervous system, bringing back intense withdrawal effects and making original anxiety roar right back.

question: Why is it important to involve local leaders right from the start of a health project?

options.A: It builds a sense of ownership and encourages community cooperation
options.B: It ensures that only the wealthiest families get treated
options.C: It stops the community from asking questions
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to do any work at all

explanation: When leaders feel involved from day one, they champion the project themselves, leading to wonderful community trust and success!

question: When doing an emergency primary survey (ABCDE), what do you check first?

options.A: Circulation
options.B: Disability
options.C: Exposure
options.D: Airway

explanation: Always start with 'A' for Airway! Making sure air can move freely into the lungs comes before anything else.

question: What is the main goal of routine health check-ups in the workplace?

options.A: To determine the exact monthly salary of each employee
options.B: To help the company fire workers who take sick leave
options.C: To diagnose unrelated personal illnesses like childhood malaria
options.D: To detect early signs of work-related illness before permanent damage occurs

explanation: Early detection is key in nursing! Routine checks catch small health issues early on, stopping them from turning into major, long-term illnesses.

question: A patient entering the diuretic stage of acute renal failure is most at risk for which complication?

options.A: Dehydration and electrolyte loss
options.B: Sudden blockage of the ureters by stones
options.C: Severe fluid overload and high blood pressure
options.D: Permanent cessation of all kidney function

explanation: In the diuretic stage, damaged nephrons start recovering and pass large amounts of fluid, which can quickly lead to dehydration if fluid isn't replaced. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h3)

question: What term describes the way the body absorbs, distributes, metabolizes, and gets rid of a drug?

options.A: Pharmacokinetics
options.B: Pathophysiology
options.C: Pharmacodynamics
options.D: Pharmaceutics

explanation: Great memory! Think of pharmacokinetics as 'what the body does to the drug' as it travels through absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion.

question: Why can unsafe formula feeding sometimes pose an even greater danger to an infant than HIV?

options.A: Contaminated water and dirty bottles cause fatal diarrhea and severe malnutrition
options.B: Commercial formula lacks basic calories needed for normal brain growth
options.C: Babies fed with formula develop immediate resistance to routine vaccines
options.D: Prepared formula breaks down the infant immune system faster than the virus

explanation: Where clean water isn't guaranteed, bad hygiene around formula bottles can cause severe tummy bugs that put a baby's life at serious risk.

question: A patient admits to taking over-the-counter stimulant laxatives every day for months. What should you advise?

options.A: Explain that daily use can cause the bowel to lose its natural function and suggest seeing a doctor
options.B: Assure the patient that daily laxative use is completely safe and healthy
options.C: Tell the patient to switch to drinking palm oil instead of taking pills
options.D: Encourage the patient to double the daily dose to get a faster result

explanation: Spot on. Relying on stimulants long-term makes the bowel lazy. Patients need professional guidance to safely restore normal habits.

question: What does an operating budget typically cover for a nursing unit?

options.A: The purchase of brand new hospital buildings and elevators
options.B: Emergency funds kept strictly for natural disasters
options.C: Long-term investments in overseas stock markets
options.D: Day-to-day expenses like staff salaries and routine medical supplies

explanation: Think of the operating budget as the money that pays for everyday running costs, like paying staff and buying routine ward supplies.

question: Which lab test specifically checks the extrinsic and common pathways of blood clotting?

options.A: Serum electrolyte panel
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Prothrombin Time (PT)
options.D: Blood urea nitrogen

explanation: PT is the go-to lab test to see how quickly the extrinsic pathway and common pathway are getting the job done.

question: What is the main reason why health insurance is so important for patients?

options.A: To provide free salaries for healthcare workers
options.B: To protect people from high out-of-pocket medical costs
options.C: To generate profits for government agencies
options.D: To completely eliminate all illnesses in a population

explanation: You got this! Health insurance acts as a financial safety net so individuals don't face financial ruin when paying for unexpected medical care.

question: Why is it best to start talking about family planning during antenatal care rather than waiting until after the baby is born?

options.A: Postpartum mothers are too tired to understand reproductive health
options.B: Hospitals forbid mothers from discussing birth control after birth
options.C: It is a legal requirement to purchase contraceptives before leaving the hospital
options.D: It gives parents adequate time to make informed choices about birth spacing

explanation: Bringing it up during ANC gives couples plenty of calm time to talk about birth spacing before the rush and exhaustion of newborn care sets in.

question: In a busy emergency unit, why do nurses grab the glucometer so quickly?

options.A: It stops the liver from making extra glucose
options.B: It proves whether the patient has diabetes permanently
options.C: It replaces the need for a full medical history
options.D: It helps spot dangerous high or low sugar levels fast

explanation: Portable glucometers give you results in seconds. Catching a dangerously high or low blood sugar early lets you step in and save the day!

question: A stable patient needs daily IV antibiotics and physical therapy after a severe foot ulcer infection. Where should they be admitted?

options.A: An intensive care unit
options.B: A subacute care facility
options.C: An outpatient primary clinic
options.D: A long-term custodial home

explanation: Exactly! Needing daily skilled nursing (like IV medications) plus active therapy fits the exact description of subacute care.

question: Which of these conditions is NOT a result of early embryonic developmental errors?

options.A: Spina bifida caused by incomplete neural tube closure
options.B: Spontaneous miscarriage due to severe chromosomal abnormalities
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed in late adulthood
options.D: Congenital heart defects from abnormal tissue septation

explanation: Type 2 diabetes is a metabolic condition related to later lifestyle and genetics, unlike birth defects caused during early pregnancy development. You're crushing it!

question: Which gland releases a hormone to raise blood calcium when it drops too low?

options.A: Parathyroid gland
options.B: Thyroid gland
options.C: Adrenal gland
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: Spot on! The tiny parathyroid glands step in with parathyroid hormone to pull calcium back into the blood when levels fall.

question: In community health, who do we usually refer to as 'stakeholders'?

options.A: Anyone with an interest or role in community health outcomes
options.B: Ministry of finance auditors from another country
options.C: Only foreign donors funding the health center
options.D: Patients who refuse to take prescribed medications

explanation: Stakeholders are simply all the key players—from local leaders and health workers to the residents themselves—who care about or are affected by the community's health.

question: Which essential vitamin is manufactured by the friendly bacteria living in our large intestine?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Vitamin K
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Vitamin D

explanation: That's correct! Our gut microbes are great roommates—they help us out by making vitamin K, which is vital for normal blood clotting.

question: What is a simple way for a nurse to spot early signs of distress in a teen client?

options.A: Measuring their exact height and weight on a growth chart
options.B: Checking their academic transcripts from school records
options.C: Testing their blood for abnormal electrolyte imbalances
options.D: Asking about changes in their daily sleep patterns and mood

explanation: Spot on! Sudden shifts in sleep or mood are classic signs that a young person might be going through emotional distress or depression. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is a key difference between benign and malignant tumors?

options.A: Malignant tumors stay completely contained within a capsule
options.B: Malignant tumors never grow back after simple removal
options.C: Benign tumors do not spread to distant parts of the body
options.D: Benign tumors always require immediate chemotherapy

explanation: A great way to remember this in the wards is that benign tumors stay put and grow slowly. Malignant tumors are the ones that can invade other tissues and spread around.

question: You get a falsely high blood pressure reading because the cuff you used was way too small for the patient's arm. What should you do next?

options.A: Record the high reading as their true baseline blood pressure
options.B: Switch to measuring the blood pressure on their ankle instead
options.C: Just subtract ten points from the result and write that down
options.D: Grab a larger cuff and repeat the check after giving the patient a short rest

explanation: A wrong cuff size means the reading isn't reliable. Always re-measure with the correct size after letting the patient rest for a minute.

question: How can nursing management figure out if communication between departments is breaking down?

options.A: Analyzing incident reports related to handoff failures
options.B: Measuring the physical temperature of hospital wards
options.C: Checking the personal social media accounts of staff
options.D: Counting the number of beds in storage

explanation: Spot on! Incident reports show managers exactly where handoffs went wrong, helping them fix those problem areas.

question: What is the primary substance used as a contrast medium during a barium swallow procedure?

options.A: Barium sulfate
options.B: Gadolinium chelate
options.C: Iodinated contrast
options.D: Normal saline

explanation: Barium sulfate is a dense, radiopaque compound that coats the lining of the digestive tract, allowing it to show up clearly on X-ray imaging. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h1)

question: What is a major reason why clients sometimes stop using modern contraceptives early?

options.A: Sudden nationwide shortages of barrier supplies
options.B: Automatic expiration of contraceptive efficacy after one month
options.C: Anxiety and fear regarding normal physiological side effects
options.D: Mandatory government limits on the duration of use

explanation: Spot on! Many clients stop using a method when they notice minor changes like spotting simply because nobody warned them it's a normal body reaction.

question: What is the primary reason for choosing soap and water over alcohol rub?

options.A: Soap and water dry out the skin much faster
options.B: Hands are visibly soiled or contaminated with spore-forming germs
options.C: Alcohol rubs are too expensive to use in general wards
options.D: Alcohol rubs take longer to apply than washing

explanation: Visible dirt and certain tough bacterial spores require the physical scrubbing action of soap, water, and friction to be removed. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: A patient asks why walking helps reduce swelling in their legs after surgery. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: Movement opens up tiny pores in your skin to evaporate excess water
options.B: Skeletal muscle contractions squeeze lymph vessels to push fluid upward
options.C: Walking directly increases the pumping strength of your heart
options.D: Walking prevents blood from entering the lower legs entirely

explanation: Because the lymphatic system lacks a heart, skeletal muscle movement is a primary driver for pushing lymph past internal valves. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which hormone does the pineal gland release to help you sleep?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: You nailed it! The pineal gland pumps out melatonin when it gets dark to help your body wind down for sleep.

question: A patient is admitted with severe heart failure and fluid accumulation in the lungs. Why is a low salt diet ordered?

options.A: To prevent further fluid retention and reduce cardiac workload
options.B: To improve digestion and absorption of oral medications
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.D: To cure the underlying viral infection in the heart muscle

explanation: Restricting salt stops the body from holding onto extra water, which lessens the volume of blood the weakened heart has to pump. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: Why must a community health profile include data on the physical environment, such as water sources?

options.A: Nurses are required by law to test the pH of every borehole in the state
options.B: Water sources directly influence the spread of waterborne infections like cholera
options.C: Environmental data determines the retirement age of community leaders
options.D: The Ministry of Water Resources pays bonuses to clinics that report rain

explanation: Unsafe drinking water is a major root cause of many infectious diseases managed at primary health care facilities. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the five core elements of post-abortion care?

options.A: Mandatory criminal investigation
options.B: Treatment of abortion complications
options.C: Contraceptive and family planning services
options.D: Post-abortion counseling

explanation: Correct! PAC is strictly about health, safety, and support—not punitive legal investigations. Our job as nurses is medical care.

question: Which of the following is a WRONG practice when using chemical safety gloves?

options.A: Wearing the exact same pair of gloves indefinitely without checking them
options.B: Inspecting the glove material for tears before starting work
options.C: Washing hands thoroughly after safely removing the gloves
options.D: Choosing glove material resistant to the specific chemical used

explanation: Well reasoned! Gloves wear out, tear, and let chemicals soak through over time. You must check them often and replace them regularly—never wear the same pair forever!

question: Which of the following women is the best candidate for a planned home delivery?

options.A: A 28-year-old with two normal past births, currently at 39 weeks with a head-first baby
options.B: A mother who experienced a severe heavy bleed after her last delivery
options.C: A 40-year-old carrying twins at 34 weeks who has severe chronic high blood pressure
options.D: A first-time mother whose baby is currently lying completely sideways in the womb

explanation: This mother has a term, single, head-first baby and a history of normal births, fitting all low-risk criteria. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h3)

question: How does promising strict privacy change how teenagers use reproductive health services?

options.A: It guarantees that teenagers will never experience health complications
options.B: It completely replaces the need for parental guidance at home
options.C: It encourages teens to seek early advice, testing, and care
options.D: It legally forces parents to abandon their teenage children

explanation: When teens know their visit is confidential, they feel safe enough to get timely checkups, contraception, or treatment when they need it. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: A nurse manager suddenly sees patient admissions double overnight. Which budgeting phase does this affect the most?

options.A: Historical auditing of past years
options.B: Initial executive board selection
options.C: Implementation and monitoring
options.D: Capital equipment depreciation

explanation: This happens during the live implementation phase, where managers constantly watch real-time patient numbers and adjust on the fly!

question: Which of these common substances acts as a Central Nervous System (CNS) depressant?

options.A: Amphetamine
options.B: Nicotine
options.C: Alcohol
options.D: Cocaine

explanation: Correct! Alcohol slows down brain activity, making it a depressant. Remember: depressants slow things down, while stimulants speed them up.

question: Why must management issue a query and hear a nurse's defense before taking disciplinary action?

options.A: To transfer the financial liability of the hospital to the nursing council
options.B: To ensure fairness, protect employee rights, and prevent arbitrary management actions
options.C: To delay disciplinary actions so that the offender can retire voluntarily
options.D: To allow the nurse to immediately apply for employment in another sector

explanation: Due process ensures everyone gets a fair hearing. Management cannot just punish you on a whim without letting you explain!

question: Which of these is a red-flag sign of a severe allergic reaction that needs instant emergency help?

options.A: Sudden facial swelling and difficulty breathing
options.B: Faint drowsiness after taking a nighttime sedative
options.C: Slight urine discoloration from a vitamin supplement
options.D: Mild dry mouth lasting for two hours

explanation: Trouble breathing and swollen lips mean anaphylaxis. That is an all-hands-on-deck emergency in the ward!

question: A nurse places a naked newborn directly onto a cold metal scale. What type of heat loss is this?

options.A: Evaporation
options.B: Radiation
options.C: Convection
options.D: Conduction

explanation: Conduction happens when the baby touches a cooler surface directly, like a cold scale. That's why we always put a warm towel down first in the ward!

question: What is 'compassion fatigue' in nursing?

options.A: Physical muscle tiredness from standing too long during a shift
options.B: Emotional exhaustion and decreased empathy from continuous exposure to patient suffering
options.C: Boredom caused by doing administrative paperwork all day
options.D: A temporary lack of sleep after working a single night shift

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when nurses absorb ongoing patient trauma without enough time to recharge, leaving them feeling emotionally drained.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended preventive action for nurses?

options.A: Identifying children at high risk during routine health visits
options.B: Performing minor cuts in the clinic to prevent severe home procedures
options.C: Collaborating with community leaders to protect young girls
options.D: Counseling families about the legal and health dangers of FGM

explanation: Nurses must never perform FGM under any circumstances, as medicalisation is unethical and illegal. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a classic ultrasound finding in someone with long-standing chronic glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Normal kidney size
options.B: Small, shrunken kidneys
options.C: A single missing kidney
options.D: Enlarged, fluid-filled cysts

explanation: Years of tissue scarring and nephron loss cause the kidneys to physically lose mass and shrink down, which doctors and sonographers easily spot on scans.

question: What is the primary operational feature of a day care centre?

options.A: Clients reside permanently within the facility grounds
options.B: Care is provided exclusively during severe medical emergencies
options.C: Children stay overnight throughout the entire week
options.D: Clients return home to their families every evening

explanation: Day care centres provide daytime supervision only, allowing clients to return home to their families at the end of each day. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h1)

question: Since newborns cannot shiver when they are cold, how do they mainly generate body heat?

options.A: By burning regular white fat under the skin
options.B: By shaking their arm and leg muscles
options.C: By sweating more on their skin
options.D: By burning special brown fat deposits

explanation: Babies have a special type of fat called 'brown adipose tissue'. Burning this fat creates heat internally without needing to shiver!

question: A patient with a spinal cord injury has frequent bladder spasms. Which drug class is the provider most likely to order?

options.A: Anticholinergics
options.B: Loop diuretics
options.C: Urinary analgesics
options.D: Antibiotics

explanation: When nerve damage causes the bladder to spasm uncontrollably, anticholinergics help relax that detrusor muscle.

question: What percentage of weight loss from pre-pregnancy weight helps nurses identify hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Loss of exactly 2 percent of body weight
options.B: Loss of more than 5 percent of body weight
options.C: Loss of up to 1 percent of body weight
options.D: Loss of 1 to 3 percent of body weight

explanation: Dropping more than 5% of her original body weight is a key sign that a mom-to-be has moved past normal morning sickness into severe hyperemesis. You've got this!

question: What is the big win of using laparoscopy instead of traditional open surgery?

options.A: General anesthesia is never required during laparoscopic pelvic procedures
options.B: It provides a clear view of internal organs without needing any camera lights
options.C: Smaller incisions lead to faster physical recovery and less postoperative pain
options.D: Patients can leave the hospital immediately before the procedure even finishes

explanation: Correct! Tiny puncture holes mean less body trauma, quicker healing, and way less pain for the patient.

question: What is the most frequent cause of acquired hypoparathyroidism?

options.A: Long-term overuse of over-the-counter antacids
options.B: A sudden bacterial infection of the bloodstream
options.C: Accidental surgical removal during neck surgery
options.D: Chronic dietary deficiency of sodium and iron

explanation: Because the parathyroid glands are so tiny and sit right next to the thyroid, they can sometimes be accidentally damaged or removed during neck surgeries.

question: What temperature range is known as the 'danger zone' where bacteria multiply quickly in food?

options.A: Zero to four degrees Celsius
options.B: Four to sixty degrees Celsius
options.C: Minus ten to zero degrees Celsius
options.D: Seventy to one hundred degrees Celsius

explanation: Between 4ÞgC and 60ÞgC, bacteria love the temperature and multiply fast. That's why perishable food shouldn't be left out too long!

question: Why is having a naturally acidic vaginal pH so important for a patient's health?

options.A: It prevents normal hormonal cycles from stopping
options.B: It stops harmful bacteria and yeast from growing
options.C: It directly digests heavy menstrual blood
options.D: It helps sperm survive longer during intercourse

explanation: Think of the acidic environment as a natural shield! Lactic acid makes it tough for bad germs to multiply and cause trouble. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is one of the key roles of a nurse when acting as a facilitator in community mobilisation?

options.A: Writing laws that fine people who refuse to visit the clinic
options.B: Helping local committees run meetings and prioritize health problems
options.C: Taking over all financial accounts of the local government
options.D: Purchasing private cars for all members of the village council

explanation: As facilitators, nurses guide the process without dominating it, helping residents make their own decisions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the medical term for the natural weakening of the immune system that happens as people get older?

options.A: Immunosenescence
options.B: Hypersensitivity
options.C: Autoimmunity
options.D: Seroconversion

explanation: Well done! 'Immuno' relates to the immune system, and 'senescence' means growing older. Put them together and you get the age-related decline in immunity.

question: Why is it best for nurses to avoid using extreme scare tactics when talking to teens about drugs?

options.A: Teens prefer lectures over friendly conversations
options.B: Exaggerated warnings are required by medical law
options.C: Teenagers see right through exaggerated claims and may lose trust in the nurse
options.D: Scare tactics instantly cure physical dependence within hours

explanation: Correct! Exaggerated warnings destroy your credibility. Teens spot fake claims easily, and once they lose trust, they stop listening altogether.

question: Why does damage to the pancreas often lead to both digestive problems and blood sugar issues?

options.A: Digestive enzymes and hormones are stored inside the exact same cells.
options.B: Insulin is required to activate all major pancreatic digestive enzymes.
options.C: The pancreas has both exocrine and endocrine functions in one organ.
options.D: The pancreas shares a direct blood supply with the liver and stomach.

explanation: You've got this! The pancreas is a multitasker. It acts as an exocrine gland to help us digest food, and an endocrine gland to manage our blood sugar. When it gets injured, both jobs take a hit.

question: What is the primary risk of poor bladder management in an immobile patient?

options.A: Liver failure
options.B: High blood pressure
options.C: Urinary tract infections
options.D: Chronic respiratory illness

explanation: Urine retention or improper catheter care easily introduces bacteria, leading to painful urinary tract infections. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h5)

question: A hospital organizes a workshop on infection control. What result best proves the training actually worked?

options.A: An increase in the number of positive comments written about the guest speaker
options.B: A higher attendance rate compared to the previous hospital seminar
options.C: A larger collection of printed handouts left behind on the empty chairs
options.D: A noticeable decrease in hospital-acquired wound infections over the next month

explanation: When infection rates drop, it proves the nurses didn't just listen—they went back to the ward and put those safety practices into action!

question: Why must you wait for the alcohol swab on a vial stopper to air dry?

options.A: Drying is required for the alcohol to kill microorganisms effectively
options.B: It prevents the needle from slipping out of your fingers
options.C: Chemicals in wet alcohol deactivate the live vaccine virus
options.D: Wet alcohol ruins the rubber stopper and causes leaks

explanation: Alcohol needs a short amount of evaporation time to disrupt cell membranes and destroy bacteria on the rubber surface. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: What is the FIRST thing you should do if a piece of equipment acts up while you are caring for a patient?

options.A: Remove the faulty item and replace it with a working one
options.B: Leave it plugged in so the next shift can look at it
options.C: Try to fix the internal wiring with electrical tape
options.D: Write an incident report for the hospital director

explanation: Patient safety comes first! Always take away the broken device and grab a working replacement right away.

question: Which type of life event is most likely to lead to complicated grief?

options.A: Sudden and violent death
options.B: Moving to a brand new neighborhood
options.C: Expected death of an elderly grandparent
options.D: Gradual retirement from work

explanation: Sudden or traumatic losses catch the mind completely off guard, making them much harder to process right away.

question: Which model explains that people change their habits by moving through steps like thinking about it, and then finally taking action?

options.A: The Biomedical Treatment Model
options.B: The Environmental Sanitation Grid
options.C: The Germ Theory of Disease
options.D: The Transtheoretical Model

explanation: Well done! The Transtheoretical Model breaks down the journey of change from early thoughts all the way to long-term maintenance.

question: Why might an elderly patient talk about tummy aches and poor appetite instead of crying when they are grieving?

options.A: Older adults often express emotional pain through physical body complaints
options.B: Physical pain always replaces sadness in older people
options.C: Grief only affects the tummy and never the brain
options.D: They are just trying to get extra attention from the nurses

explanation: Spot on! Older adults often show emotional hurt through physical signs, known as somatic symptoms. Always keep an eye out for this in clinical practice.

question: A village is turning down a new immunization drive because of heavy rumors. What should you do first?

options.A: Ignore the rumors and continue vaccinating those who show up voluntarily
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders and local influencers to discuss concerns
options.C: Report the community to security forces for refusing public health care
options.D: Cancel the immunization program and shift supplies to urban centers

explanation: Exactly! Working through respected local figures is the best way to clear up misunderstandings, answer questions, and build genuine trust.

question: How should a nurse handle a cultural food taboo that limits a pregnant woman's protein intake?

options.A: Ignore the food taboo completely and focus only on vitamin supplements
options.B: Provide respectful education while suggesting nutritious local alternatives
options.C: Mock the cultural belief to force the patient into immediate compliance
options.D: Report the family to local community authorities for traditional practices

explanation: Respectful dialogue and culturally sensitive education work best to address harmful myths without alienating the patient or community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h5)

question: Which of the following is a major systemic challenge facing health promotion programs in Nigeria?

options.A: An extreme surplus of modern medical equipment in rural areas
options.B: Too many well-funded hospitals with no patients to treat
options.C: Brain drain of skilled healthcare professionals leaving the country
options.D: Zero interest from local communities in improving their health

explanation: The migration of experienced doctors and nurses abroad significantly weakens local healthcare delivery systems and health promotion efforts. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)

question: As a nurse, which common transport mistake should you always avoid?

options.A: Checking patient identification labels against the laboratory request forms
options.B: Wearing clean gloves while handling outside surfaces of specimen tubes
options.C: Assuming standard hospital trash bags are sufficient for off-site transport
options.D: Wiping down secondary containers if a minor drop of fluid touches the outside

explanation: Regular waste bags are not strong enough or certified for road transport. Always use approved UN-certified packaging for safety!

question: What is 'member checking' when doing qualitative research?

options.A: Sharing findings back with participants to confirm accuracy
options.B: Testing the audio recorder battery before an interview
options.C: Reviewing staff membership lists for the research team
options.D: Checking if participants paid their hospital bills

explanation: Brilliant! Member checking means going back to your participants to say, 'Did I get your story right?' It ensures your interpretation is honest and true.

question: If you visit a home and suspect a vulnerable client is being abused, what is your primary duty?

options.A: Wait until you have absolute proof before telling anyone
options.B: Confront the suspected family member aggressively during the visit
options.C: Report your suspicion immediately to the proper protective authorities
options.D: Keep it a secret to protect family relationships

explanation: Correct! When dealing with vulnerable clients, your priority is their safety. Report suspicions right away so the right agencies can step in.

question: Why are neonates especially vulnerable to drug toxicity?

options.A: Immature liver enzymes and undeveloped kidney filtration
options.B: An unusually high metabolic rate that burns up medications
options.C: A complete lack of blood circulation to internal organs
options.D: Increased total body fat that traps water-soluble drugs

explanation: Babies cannot break down and excrete drugs efficiently because their organs are still developing. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the main reason for putting a Plaster of Paris cast on a broken bone?

options.A: To immobilize the bone ends for proper healing
options.B: To dissolve small bone fragments inside the muscle
options.C: To increase local blood circulation to the tissue
options.D: To deliver topical antibiotics directly to the skin

explanation: Spot on! The cast holds the broken bone steady so it can fuse back together correctly without shifting.

question: How should a patient breathe while receiving nasal drop medication?

options.A: By holding their breath
options.B: With deep chest breaths
options.C: Through their mouth
options.D: Slowly through their nose

explanation: Breathing through the mouth prevents the patient from accidentally inhaling the drops down into their lungs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is the main goal of community nursing surveillance when it comes to poisons and toxic substances?

options.A: To replace the need for community health education
options.B: To detect patterns or outbreaks of poisoning early
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of chemical imports
options.D: To punish factories that fail safety inspections

explanation: Spot on! Tracking poison cases helps public health teams spot trends quickly, allowing us to step in and save lives before more people get hurt.

question: What is another common name for a scatter diagram?

options.A: Scatter plot
options.B: Pie chart
options.C: Line histogram
options.D: Bar graph

explanation: A scatter diagram is also widely known as a scatter plot because it plots individual data points across a grid. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why is bone considered an important storage bank for the whole body?

options.A: It burns stored fat tissue to maintain a stable body temperature
options.B: It produces hormones that regulate the speed of digestion
options.C: It filters waste products directly out of the circulating blood supply
options.D: It stores large amounts of essential minerals like calcium and phosphorus

explanation: Bones hold onto key minerals and release them into the blood whenever your nerves and muscles need them. Perfect!

question: Which patients in a hospital setting require the use of standard precautions?

options.A: All patients regardless of their diagnosis
options.B: Patients admitted to surgical wards only
options.C: Only patients who have open wounds
options.D: Only patients with confirmed infectious diseases

explanation: Standard precautions are designed for every patient interaction because infection status is not always known upon admission. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: When should a nurse document that a medication has been given to a patient?

options.A: Immediately after the patient swallows the medication
options.B: Before pouring the medication from the stock bottle
options.C: At the end of the entire nursing shift
options.D: Whenever the nurse has spare time during the day

explanation: Documenting right after administration prevents accidental double-dosing and ensures an accurate, up-to-date medical record. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h8)

question: Which food group is most helpful to prevent constipation in older adults who aren't very active?

options.A: Simple sugars
options.B: Animal proteins
options.C: Dietary fiber
options.D: Saturated fats

explanation: Great thinking! Fiber adds bulk to stool and keeps things moving smoothly, helping make up for slower digestion in older age.

question: Why is data analysis a critical step before planning any healthcare intervention?

options.A: It allows nurses to guess which disease is causing trouble without proof
options.B: It turns raw numbers into clear insights so the real problems become visible
options.C: It ensures that all health funding goes directly into hospital building projects
options.D: It stops community members from expressing their personal opinions

explanation: Without analysis, data remains a confusing pile of numbers that cannot guide effective action. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of these conditions is NOT linked to problems in the limbic system?

options.A: Major depressive disorder
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Correct! Iron deficiency anemia is a blood and nutrition issue, whereas anxiety, depression, and PTSD are all tied to limbic system imbalances.

question: How do cultural misconceptions about disabilities directly impact a special child?

options.A: They motivate rapid medical diagnosis in rural clinics
options.B: They improve community volunteer participation
options.C: They often lead families to hide the child away due to shame or fear
options.D: They guarantee immediate government scholarship awards

explanation: Superstitious beliefs and heavy stigma can cause families to conceal children, keeping them away from the medical and social support they deserve.

question: A patient with severe ascites is struggling to breathe. How does draining the fluid help?

options.A: It stops the heart from beating too quickly
options.B: It directly opens up the blocked airways in the lungs
options.C: It lowers the diaphragm and lets the lungs expand
options.D: It pumps extra oxygen directly into the bloodstream

explanation: When too much fluid pushes up against the diaphragm, the lungs can't expand fully. Removing it gives the lungs room to breathe again!

question: How does the placenta give a newborn temporary protection against common infections?

options.A: By actively transferring maternal IgG antibodies across the placental membrane
options.B: By producing white blood cells that migrate into the fetal bloodstream
options.C: By filtering out all bacteria and viruses from maternal blood
options.D: By stimulating the fetal bone marrow to produce immunoglobulins

explanation: Nature's gift! The placenta lets the mother's protective IgG antibodies pass through to the baby, giving them a helpful head start against infections after birth.

question: What is a major health risk for a teenage athlete who consistently eats far fewer calories than their body burns?

options.A: Excessive increases in height growth
options.B: Instant muscle hypertrophy and strength gains
options.C: Delayed puberty and poor bone health
options.D: Improved long-term cardiovascular immunity

explanation: When growing teens don't get enough fuel, their hormone balance gets upset, which can delay puberty and weaken their bones.

question: A nurse wonders if a self-care theory works for elderly patients in rural farming communities. Where does this research idea come from?

options.A: Biomedical laboratory equipment maintenance
options.B: Professional theories and conceptual frameworks
options.C: Hospital financial accounting records
options.D: Direct pharmaceutical marketing campaigns

explanation: Testing established nursing models on new groups of people is a fantastic way to grow our professional knowledge.

question: A clinic nurse notices an unusual rise in severe watery diarrhea cases over two days. What should she do first?

options.A: Wait another month to see if the patient numbers drop on their own
options.B: Prescribe strong antibiotics to everyone living in the local village
options.C: Close the clinic permanently to prevent any further infections
options.D: Report the unusual cluster to public health authorities for investigation

explanation: You nailed it! Catching unusual symptom clusters early and reporting them helps stop outbreaks like cholera right in their tracks.

question: Which baby outcome is most common in pregnancies among very young adolescents?

options.A: Childhood developmental hyperactive disorders
options.B: Macrosomia and post-term delivery
options.C: Low birth weight and prematurity
options.D: Congenital bone malformations

explanation: Because the young mother's body is still developing and sharing nutrients, babies are often born early and weigh less than normal.

question: A patient who eats a strict vegan diet and avoids all animal products is most at risk of lacking which nutrient?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: Vitamin B12 is mostly found in animal foods like meat, eggs, and dairy. Strict vegans often need to take a supplement to keep their B12 levels healthy.

question: Why do nurses ask about a patient's job or daily work during a bone and muscle assessment?

options.A: To identify repetitive physical movements that may cause injury
options.B: To check if they can afford prescribed orthopedic devices
options.C: To find out if they have health insurance coverage
options.D: To determine their exact monthly income for hospital billing

explanation: Work habits and daily physical tasks heavily influence joint and muscle strain over time. Great job thinking about the whole patient!

question: What is a normal, expected feeling for a patient right after a sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: Mild belly bloating and the need to pass gas
options.B: Severe, sharp pain all over the stomach
options.C: Total numbness in both legs
options.D: An inability to pee for 24 hours

explanation: That's right! The air pumped into the bowel during the test has to come out somehow, causing temporary gas and bloating.

question: What is the primary function of luteinizing hormone in the male reproductive system?

options.A: Stimulating testosterone production in the testes
options.B: Directly forming the flagellum of maturing sperm
options.C: Neutralizing acidic fluid in the male urethra
options.D: Lowering body temperature inside the scrotal sac

explanation: Luteinizing hormone targets specific cells in the testes to trigger the synthesis and release of testosterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h3)

question: How does a new mother's body get rid of extra pregnancy fluid in the first few days after birth?

options.A: Diuresis and diaphoresis
options.B: Bleeding from the placental site
options.C: Severe vomiting and diarrhea
options.D: Rapid breathing through the lungs

explanation: Spot on! The body naturally flushes out the extra fluid through heavy passing of urine and sweating.

question: Which supportive procedure is commonly used to give the bowel a rest during an acute GI crisis?

options.A: Early heavy oral feeding
options.B: Nasogastric tube insertion
options.C: Daily strenuous exercise
options.D: High-fiber meal planning

explanation: Spot on! An NG tube suctions out stomach contents and gas, which lets the bowel rest and prevents further pressure or vomiting. You are building up great practical knowledge!

question: What is the primary reason for proper healthcare waste management?

options.A: To make hospital compounds look neat
options.B: To create more space in the wards
options.C: To reduce the cost of hospital cleaning
